polityNote: The Dominion of India from independence (15 August 1947) to the day before the Constitution (26 January 1950; from then IND.json). Atoms: geoBoundaries ADM3 of IND (2018 subdistricts), the set BRI-provinces-1937.json uses to 14 August 1947, and the same unions where the provinces kept their lines. Only the ground no dated record answers is drawn — the United Provinces with Rampur and Tehri Garhwal as they merged, Delhi, the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and Cochin; OpenHistoricalMap draws West Bengal, Assam, Bihar, Orissa, Madras, Mysore, East Punjab and the unions of states on these dates (test 4). Bombay and the Central India states stay unresolved: the states were interleaved and merged piecemeal, and the enclaves were exchanged only on 26 January 1950.

unresolved.what: Benares State (Bhadohi and Chakia)
unresolved.why: The date the state merged into the United Provinces is not established: Wikipedia «Benares State» gives 1948 in its categories and 1949 in its infobox, statoids lists it under 15 August 1947, and no day is stated.
unresolved.needs: the merger agreement or the UP notification creating Bhadohi/Chakia tehsils

unresolved.what: Hyderabad State (Telangana and Hyderabad Karnataka subdistricts)
unresolved.why: Hyderabad did not accede in 1947 and was taken under Indian military administration on 18 September 1948 (OpenHistoricalMap draws it from that day); before 26 January 1950 it exchanged enclaves with Bombay, Madras and the Central Provinces, so its outline before that day is not a line of today’s mandals.
unresolved.needs: the pre-1950 enclaves as village atoms

unresolved.what: Bombay Province and the Bombay, Gujarat and Deccan states
unresolved.why: British districts and several hundred states were interleaved; 174 states merged into Bombay piecemeal in 1948–49 (Baroda on 1 May 1949) while Saurashtra and Kutch formed separately, and the enclaves between Bombay, Hyderabad, Madras and the Central Provinces were exchanged only on 26 January 1950 — no union of today’s talukas carries Bombay’s line before 1950. OpenHistoricalMap draws Bombay from 24 January 1950, Baroda, Kolhapur, Kutch and Saurashtra for parts of the period.
unresolved.needs: the states’ village lists and the 1950 enclave order as village atoms

unresolved.what: Central Provinces and Berar, the Central India states, Gwalior, Bhopal and the Chhattisgarh states
unresolved.why: The Central India states were interleaved at village level until the unions of 1948 (Vindhya Pradesh 12 March, Madhya Bharat 28 May; Bhopal centrally administered from 1 June 1949) and the 1950 enclave order; OpenHistoricalMap draws the Central Provinces and Berar, Gwalior and the unions.
unresolved.needs: the states’ village lists as atoms

unresolved.what: Jammu and Kashmir
unresolved.why: The state had not acceded until 26 October 1947; OpenHistoricalMap draws Jammu and Kashmir from that day, with the line of actual control of 1949 that today’s subdistricts do not carry.

unresolved.what: Laccadive, Minicoy and Amindivi Islands
unresolved.why: Parts of the Malabar and South Kanara districts of Madras until 1 November 1956; whether OpenHistoricalMap’s Madras includes the islands was not established, and they are left with Madras.

unresolved.what: The hills beyond the Outer Line (North-East Frontier Tracts, today’s Arunachal Pradesh)
unresolved.why: Tribal areas administered by the Governor of Assam; their extent against the Assam districts and the era map’s northern line are not established for 1947–50.
unresolved.needs: the 1950 schedule of the tribal areas (Sixth Schedule, Part B) as atoms

unresolved.what: Khasi and Jaintia Hills (the Khasi states and British villages)
unresolved.why: The Khasi states and the British villages were interleaved (BRI-provinces-1937.json); OpenHistoricalMap’s Assam Province answers the ground on these dates.

unresolved.what: Bagepalli taluk and its Andhra neighbours
unresolved.why: One survey number was transferred from Mysore to Andhra Pradesh on 1 October 1968; today's units on both sides differ from the earlier line by that survey number.
unresolved.needs: village atoms of Bagepalli taluk

unresolved.what: Banganapalle state and the mandals around it (Kurnool)
unresolved.why: The state became part of Kurnool district in 1948 and its outline is not a line of today's mandals.
unresolved.needs: the state's village list

unresolved.what: Bhadrachalam and Nugur taluks (Madras, Godavari district) against Paloncha (Hyderabad)
unresolved.why: Bhadrachalam moved to Khammam in 1959 and seven mandals back to Andhra Pradesh in 2014 (with part of Burgampahad); today's mandals on both banks mix the two sides.
checked: mandal list of Bhadradri Kothagudem, Mulugu and the 2014-transferred mandals
unresolved.needs: village lists of the 1959 and 2014 transfers

unresolved.what: Bihar–United Provinces line on the Ganga, Ghaghra and Gandak
unresolved.why: The line follows shifting rivers and was re-fixed by the Bihar and Uttar Pradesh (Alteration of Boundaries) Act 1968, which moved riverine villages both ways; today's blocks on either bank therefore do not carry the 1886–1947 line.
checked: adjacency of today's blocks/tehsils along the Bihar–UP line
unresolved.needs: village (mauza) boundaries of the riverine diara before 1968

unresolved.what: United Provinces districts of Bundelkhand (Jhansi, Lalitpur, Jalaun, Hamirpur, Mahoba, Banda, Chitrakoot)
unresolved.why: These British districts were interleaved with Central India states and jagirs (Samthar, Charkhari, Sarila, Baoni, the Chaube jagirs …), and their enclaves were absorbed in 1950; today's tehsils mix British and state ground. The Bundelkhand states joined Vindhya Pradesh in 1948 but the enclaves were exchanged only on 26 January 1950.
checked: tehsil list of the seven districts
unresolved.needs: the 1950 absorption-of-enclaves schedules or pre-1947 village maps

unresolved.what: Chandernagore (French) inside the Singur block of Hooghly
unresolved.why: The French enclave is not a separate atom in the gb dataset (point-in-polygon of Chandannagar falls in «Singur»). Chandernagore was transferred de facto on 2 May 1950, after this scope.
unresolved.needs: Chandannagar municipal boundary as an atom

unresolved.what: Taluks on the Cochin–Malabar and Cochin–Travancore lines (Chittur, Alathur, Chavakkad, Kunnamkulam, all Ernakulam taluks)
unresolved.why: Each mixes Cochin with Malabar or Travancore villages (Wikipedia: parts of Alathur, Kochi less Fort Kochi, Kanayannur less Edappally, parts of Aluva); Chittur, said to be wholly Cochin, measures 1,151 km², far above the state's Chittur taluk.
unresolved.needs: village atoms of these taluks

unresolved.what: Cooch Behar state and the chhitmahal belt (Cooch Behar, the adjoining Jalpaiguri/Alipurduar blocks, and Panchagarh, Nilphamari, Lalmonirhat, Bhurungamari and Phulbari in Bangladesh)
unresolved.why: Cooch Behar state and Rangpur/Jalpaiguri held about 200 enclaves in each other until the 2015 exchange; today's blocks and upazilas absorbed them, so none carries the state line. Cooch Behar merged with West Bengal on 1 January 1950; the enclaves remained until 31 July 2015.
unresolved.needs: chhitmahal polygons before 2015

unresolved.what: Karandighi block (Uttar Dinajpur)
unresolved.why: It lies in the Islampur subdivision that came from Bihar (Purnea) in 1956, but the Dalkhola police station spans parts of Karandighi and Goalpokhar II, so whether the whole block was Purnea or partly Dinajpur is not established; the 1905–1947 provincial line may run through it.
unresolved.needs: the 1956 transfer schedule (Bihar and West Bengal (Transfer of Territories) Act 1956)

unresolved.what: Khariar (today's Nuapada district)
unresolved.why: Khariar zamindari was in the Central Provinces (drawn by OpenHistoricalMap) until 1936 and then in Orissa; its extent against today's Nuapada district is not established.
unresolved.needs: the 1936 transfer schedule

unresolved.what: Munagala pargana (a Krishna-district enclave in Nalgonda)
unresolved.why: The Madras enclave was transferred to Nalgonda after 1956; its outline against today's Munagala and Nadigudem mandals is not established.
unresolved.needs: the enclave's village list

unresolved.what: gb IND ADM3 feature «Lm» without geometry
unresolved.why: The dataset carries this feature with no polygon; it cannot be drawn.
unresolved.needs: a polygon for the feature

unresolved.what: Subdistricts of coastal Orissa touching the tributary states
unresolved.why: The Orissa tributary states were merged into Orissa in 1948–49 and their lines with the British districts are not proven to coincide with today's police-station lines.
checked: adjacency of today's units to the state districts
unresolved.needs: the 1949 merger schedules or pre-1948 village maps

unresolved.what: Pudukkottai state and Aranthangi taluk (today's Pudukkottai district)
unresolved.why: Wikipedia says the state was the whole district except Aranthangi taluk, but the nine non-Aranthangi taluks measure 3,560 km² against the state's 1,178 sq mi (3,051 km²); the line is not established at taluk level.
unresolved.needs: the 1948 merger schedule

unresolved.what: Ramnagar (Benares State) inside Varanasi Sadar tehsil
unresolved.why: Ramnagar was part of Benares State from 1911 while the rest of the tehsil was British; the tehsil cannot be split.
unresolved.needs: village atoms of Varanasi Sadar

unresolved.what: Rudraprayag district (formed 1997)
unresolved.why: Formed from parts of Chamoli and Pauri (British Garhwal) and of Tehri district (Tehri state); its tehsils straddle the state line.
unresolved.needs: block-level origin of Rudraprayag

unresolved.what: Sandur state (inside Sandur taluk)
unresolved.why: The state (161 sq mi) is far smaller than today's Sandur taluk (1,248 km²); its line runs inside the taluk.
unresolved.needs: the state's village list

unresolved.what: Saraikela and Kharsawan states (today's Saraikela-Kharsawan district)
unresolved.why: The district joins the two tributary states with the Chandil, Ichagarh, Nimdih and Kukru areas of British Manbhum; which blocks were which is not established.
unresolved.needs: block-level origin of Saraikela-Kharsawan district

unresolved.what: Uttarkashi district
unresolved.why: The state held «most of» today's Uttarkashi district; which part lay outside is not established.
unresolved.needs: the 1949 merger schedule or a pre-1949 map of the state

unresolved.what: Punjab–United Provinces line on the Yamuna
unresolved.why: The Haryana and Uttar Pradesh (Alteration of Boundaries) Act 1979 re-fixed the Yamuna line; tehsils on the UP bank no longer carry the colonial line.
unresolved.needs: village boundaries along the Yamuna before 1979
